installer_meta.maintainer_note: Community-maintained (exotic edition). Void's zfs package builds its module with DKMS on the machine; here it comes prebuilt instead, as linux6.18-zfs from freedomnas-void, the xbps repository FreedomNAS publishes on Codeberg, which also holds the FreedomNAS packages themselves (installer_meta.core_packages), in the group of the installer's channel (files.xbps_freedomnas, signed with the key in files.xbps_freedomnas_key). ignorepkg=dkms keeps zfs from pulling DKMS, gcc and the headers in; ignorepkg=linux lets repositories.core remove the linux meta package base-system brings, which would move to a kernel series with no module yet: packages/core.json names the series (linux6.18), and it has to change together with freedomnas-void's series file. Void runs /etc/kernel.d/post-install hooks, not /etc/kernel/postinst.d, so files.freedomnas_uki_hook calls zz-dracut-uki from there, and only once zfs.ko is in place: linux6.18-zfs runs the hooks again after installing it. The tarball method uses Void's own ROOTFS tarball, whose filename is date-stamped, so rootfs_tarball_url is left empty on purpose and the installer asks for it.

rootpool.create: zpool create {force} -o ashift={ashift} -O acltype=posixacl -O canmount=off -O compression={compression} -O dnodesize=auto -O normalization=formD -O relatime=on -O xattr=sa -O mountpoint=/ -R {altroot} {pool_name} {device}

xbps_keys.content:
set -eu
root="$1"
keys=/var/db/xbps/keys
mkdir -p "$root$keys"
if ls "$keys"/*.plist >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    cp "$keys"/*.plist "$root$keys"/
    exit 0
fi
static="$(echo "$2" | sed 's|/current/*$||')/static"
dir="$(dirname "$0")"
curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o "$dir/sha256sums.txt" "$static/sha256sums.txt"
name="$(sed -n 's/^[0-9a-f]*  \(xbps-static-static-[0-9][^ ]*\.{arch}-musl\.tar\.xz\)$/\1/p' "$dir/sha256sums.txt" | sort -V | tail -n1)"
[ -n "$name" ] || {{ echo "xbps-keys: no xbps-static tarball listed at $static" >&2; exit 1; }}
curl -fsSL --retry 3 -o "$dir/$name" "$static/$name"
(cd "$dir" && grep "  $name\$" sha256sums.txt | sha256sum -c --quiet -)
tar -xJf "$dir/$name" -C "$root" --no-same-owner ./var/db/xbps/keys

core: if xbps-query linux >/dev/null 2>&1; then xbps-remove -y linux; fi

dracut_uki.content:
# The UKI is built inside a chroot, where dracut's idea of "this host" is
# the installer's, not the machine being installed.
hostonly="no"
# Wait for the root pool before importing it (assets/dracut/
# 91freedomnas-rootwait): a USB stick appears after the zfs module tries.
add_dracutmodules+=" freedomnas-rootwait freedomnas-fallback "
# dracut 111 (Arch/Artix) installs nothing for its "=drivers/<dir>" module
# lists, so an image booted from a USB stick has no usb-storage/uas to find
# its root pool and no USB keyboard in the rescue shell. Name the modules of
# those directories explicitly instead; dracut sets $kernel before reading
# this file.
add_drivers+=" $(find /lib/modules/"$kernel"/kernel/drivers/usb/storage /lib/modules/"$kernel"/kernel/drivers/usb/host /lib/modules/"$kernel"/kernel/drivers/hid /lib/modules/"$kernel"/kernel/drivers/input/keyboard /lib/modules/"$kernel"/kernel/drivers/input/serio /lib/modules/"$kernel"/kernel/drivers/mmc -name '*.ko*' -printf '%f\n' 2>/dev/null | sed 's/\.ko.*$//') "
# base-system installs every linux-firmware package, so dracut's drm module
# would carry ~150 MB of GPU firmware (NVIDIA's alone is 110 MB) into each
# UKI and the ESP could not hold them. A NAS needs no GPU driver to boot:
# the console stays on the firmware's framebuffer.
omit_dracutmodules+=" drm "

fstab.content:
# /etc/fstab - ZFS datasets are mounted by ZFS, not fstab
{esp_spec}	/boot/efi	vfat	defaults	0	2

scheduled_jobs.content:
# FreedomNAS scheduled work. Cron decides when; config.yaml decides what,
# so a system with no policies costs a handful of no-ops a day.
PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
PYTHONPATH={install_root}/core
0  * * * *  root  python3 -m freedomnas snapshot-run --interval hourly  >> /var/log/freedomnas-scheduled.log 2>&1
5  0 * * *  root  python3 -m freedomnas snapshot-run --interval daily   >> /var/log/freedomnas-scheduled.log 2>&1
10 0 * * 0  root  python3 -m freedomnas snapshot-run --interval weekly  >> /var/log/freedomnas-scheduled.log 2>&1
15 0 1 * *  root  python3 -m freedomnas snapshot-run --interval monthly >> /var/log/freedomnas-scheduled.log 2>&1
# The configuration's shadow copy on every other pool: what a reinstall
# onto a blank disk finds waiting for it on the data pool.
30 3 * * *  root  python3 -m freedomnas shadow-sync                     >> /var/log/freedomnas-scheduled.log 2>&1

sudoers.content:
# FreedomNAS: the WebUI runs updates as the signed-in user,
# and topgrade calls sudo itself for the steps that need root.
%{sudo_group} ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL

xbps_freedomnas.content:
# FreedomNAS: its own packages, and OpenZFS modules built for Void's kernel,
# from freedomnas-void, so that zfs needs no DKMS here, and no linux meta
# package, which would move to a kernel series before its module is published.
repository=https://codeberg.org/api/packages/FreedomNAS/generic/freedomnas-void/{channel}
ignorepkg=dkms
ignorepkg=linux

xbps_freedomnas_key.content:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple Computer//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
	<key>public-key</key>
	<data></data>
	<key>public-key-size</key>
	<integer>4096</integer>
	<key>signature-by</key>
	<string>FreedomNAS</string>
</dict>
</plist>

freedomnas_uki_hook.content:
#!/bin/sh
# Void runs /etc/kernel.d/post-install/* with the package name and the kernel
# version, never /etc/kernel/postinst.d, so the UKI is rebuilt from here.
# Without zfs.ko the UKI would not boot: until linux<series>-zfs has put it
# in place, do nothing; that package runs these hooks again afterwards, so
# the UKI is built, and rotated into the rollback slot, once per kernel.
[ -x /etc/kernel/postinst.d/zz-dracut-uki ] || exit 0
[ -f /usr/lib/modules/$2/extra/zfs.ko ] || exit 0
exec /etc/kernel/postinst.d/zz-dracut-uki "$2"

freedomnas_uki_backup_hook.content:
#!/bin/sh
# Before a kernel is installed, the running UKI goes to the rollback slot.
[ -x /etc/kernel/postinst.d/zz-dracut-uki ] || exit 0
exec /etc/kernel/postinst.d/zz-dracut-uki --backup
